technical-data.invention-title: CUTTING TOOL FOR PARTING AND SIMILAR OPERATIONS
OUTIL DE COUPE POUR DES OPERATIONS DE SEPARATION ET ANALOGUES

abstract.p: The present invention relates to a tool for parting or similar blade type operations, comprising a holder in the shape of a blade portion (1) and a cutting insert (2), said blade portion (1) having at least one free end with an outwardly open recess (4) and a rear slot (8), said recess being confined by a bottom wall (5), an inner or rear wall (6) and an upper wall (7) which is part of an elastic movable clamping arm (3) integral with said blade portion to fasten the insert into the recess. The characteristic feature of the invention is the arrangement of a rear support wall in the shape of a support surface (6) which in relation to the bottom wall (5) extends upwards and in its upper part extends into a convexly curved surface (14) with relatively large radius (R1) which extends into a partial surface (15) with essentially smaller radius (R2) which at an inflexion point (16) extends into a concave curved surface (8a) which defines the end of the rear slot (8).

La présente invention concerne un outil servant à effectuer des opérations de séparation ou autres du type à lame, comprenant un support en forme de partie lame (1) et une pièce coupante rapportée (2). La partie lame (1) possède au moins une extrémité libre dotée d'un évidement ouvert vers l'extérieur (4) et d'une fente arrière (8), ledit évidement étant délimité par une paroi inférieure (5), une paroi interne ou arrière (6) et une paroi supérieure (7) faisant partie d'un segment de préhension (3) mobile de manière élastique, monobloc avec la partie lame et servant à bloquer la pièce rapportée dans l'évidement. L'aspect caractéristique de l'invention est constitué par la présence d'une paroi de support arrière ayant la forme d'une surface de support (6) s'étendant vers le haut par rapport à la paroi inférieure et qui, dans sa partie supérieure, présente une surface convexe (14) de rayon (R1) relativement grand qui se prolonge en une surface partielle (15) de rayon (R2) sensiblement inférieur qui, en un point d'inflexion (16) se prolonge en une surface concave (8a) définissant l'extrémité de la fente arrière (8).

description.p: Cutting tool for parting and similar operations

The present invention relates to a tool for parting or similar turning operations of the type which includes a holder in the shape of a rather thin disc or disc-shaped member of a first material, such as steel, and a cutting insert of a second harder material, such as cemented carbide, wherein at least the front portion of said holder blade is provided with an outwardly open recess. The recess is mainly defined by a lower bottom surface, an inner or rear wall and an upper wall integral with an elastically flexible arm intended to clamp the insert into its recess, whereby the insert has both upper and lower V-shaped grooves or ridges intended to cooperate with correspondingly V-shaped ridges or recesses in connection with said recess.

During repeated parting and grooving it is of special importance that the tool has a well defined axial support against which the rear end of the insert can be supported. It is another demand that the height of said surface is not too large so as to cause damaging surface contact with a zone close to the active corner of the cutting insert in case of using double-ended inserts. One of the drawbacks with the present commonly used blade holders is that they do not provide an appropriate axial support to more than one type of inserts. Each time when the operator needs to change inserts to another type with another type of cutting portion having another inclination angle at the clearance surface below the cutting edge he must also change blade holder. Hence, there is a need of a new type of blade holder suitable to receive several different types of inserts.

The present invention relates to a new type of blade holder wherein the insert-receiving recess of the holder comprises a rear axial support with such formation that insert with widely varying inclination angles of the clearance surface below the cutting edge can be received therein. The features specific for the invention will be defined more in detail by reference to the enclosed drawings. These are now briefly presented:
In the drawings:
Fig. 1 is a partial perspective view of a cutting tool of the invention with an insert mounted in place in a blade shaped holder.
Fig. 2 is a side view of the tool of Fig. 1.
Fig. 3 is a side view of the blade holder of Fig. 1-2 without any insert.
Fig. 4 is a perspective enlarged view of the bottom and inner walls of the insert receiving recess, and
Fig. 5 is an enlarged view showing the insert after being mounted into the tool.

The parting tool of Fig. 1 comprises a blade type holder, in its entirety designated 1, and a cutting insert 2. The insert 2 can in certain cases be supported against a separate shim plate (not shown). The holder 1 is in the shape of a rather thin disc or blade shaped portion made of steel or similar material. In practice said blade holder is often rectangular, elongated, and has at least one of its opposite ends provided with an upper clamp arm 3 integral with the holder whilst having an outwardly open recess 4 (see Fig. 3) which is mainly confined by a bottom wall 5, an inner or rear wall 6 and an upper wall 7 which is part of the elastic movable clamp arm 3 of said blade holder provided to fasten the insert into its recess. In the embodiment shown as example in the drawings the blade holder 1 has a slot 8 the end of which is smoothly rounded. The purpose of this slot is to provide a certain amount of elasticity to the clamp arm 3 and to provide a certain space for the cutting edge and the insert portion below said cutting edge such that damaging surface contact not appears. The arm 3 could alternatively, due to its resilience, in a manner known per se, be pivoted downwards towards the bottom wall of the recess by means of a separate clamp screw (not shown).

The insert 2 as shown in Fig. 1-2 is made of a cemented carbide body the front end of which has a main cutting edge 9, next to which there is provided a chip breaker surface
10 on the upper surface of said body. In the area behind the chip breaking portion 10 there is a raised portion of said insert body that is provided with a recess 11 V-shaped in cross-section divided in forward and rear portions 11 ' and 11 " respectively between which there is a central groove with concave rounded form (not shown). The underneath side of said insert body 2 is also provided with a groove 12 V-shaped in cross-section. In practice both grooves on said upper and lower sides could have an identical V-shaped formation.

Although the cutting edge 9 in the example as shown extends perpendicular to the longitudinal extension of the insert the form and location of the edge could be widely varied. The insert can be provided with circularly rounded or partially rounded edges and when the edge is straight it could be inclined in relation to the longitudinal extent of the insert.

According to the invention the insert 2 is arranged to be supported against a rear upstanding wall 6 that is integral with the blade holder in said recess. This support wall 6 extends via a convexly curved surface into a curved end portion made by groove milling into the rear slot 8. The detailed embodiment is preferably such that the rear portion of the bottom wall 5 extends into a milled groove 5a with smoothly rounded contour, which then extends into the support wall 6 approximately at the inflexion point 13. By this embodiment it is ensured that both the rear, lower and upper edge portions of the insert become freely exposed from said blade holder. The upstanding support wall 6 can be planar, preferably with a height less than its width whereby said support wall 6 only needs to have a relatively limited height extension as shown in Fig. 4. Alternatively, however, the rear insert surface that is intended for contact with said support wall 6 could be provided with a V-shaped recess and the support wall 6 can have a male extension such that said extension and said V-shaped groove are provided as a joint of male means and female means.

As best appears from Fig. 5, the detailed embodiment is such that the axial support wall 6 extends upwards and extends into a convexly shaped transition surface 14 of relatively large radius Ri which extends into a convex partial surface 15 with essentially smaller
radius R . This partial surface 15 then extends into groove 8 confined by a surface 8a with a radius R3 which in this shown embodiment is larger than both above mentioned radii Ri and R2. In certain cases, however, Rj could be larger than R3. The radius R3 ought to be equal to or preferably larger than radius R of said groove 5a. Thanks to this embodiment it is possible to receive in the same blade holder the insert 2 shown in Fig. 1-3 the rear end surface of which comprises a lower end surface 2a on the insert that extends perpendicularly from the bottom wall 5 and an upper clearance surface 2b. This last mentioned clearance surface 2b is hereby freely exposed from the rear support wall 6. In the same holder can also be received an insert with the form having the dashed appearance N as shown in Fig. 5. As appears from Fig. 5 this insert has a form that deviates both in its lower and upper portion. Thus, lower surface portion A, of said dashed appearance A has an acute clearance angle that amounts to 45° whereas the upper surface portion A2 has been provided with a substantially smaller clearance angle β. In spite of these geometrical differences this insert can be well received in same blade holder as the insert shown in Fig. 1-2. The reason is that the lower sharply inclined clearance surface A2 can have an appropriate support against the upper portion of the convexly shaped surface 16. The size of Ri ought to be in the range 0.2-100 mm, preferably 0.5-5 mm whereas R ought to be in the range 0-10 mm, preferably 0.2-2 mm. The size of R3 ought to be 0.2-10 mm, preferably 0.2-5 mm whereas the size of R4 ought to be 0.5-5 mm, preferably 1-5 mm.

The number of blade holders can hereby be essentially reduced for a customer that needs a number of differently shaped inserts depending upon which type of grooving and type of workpiece material to be used which is a commonly occurring situation in the machining industry.

Various embodiments of the above example can of course be used within the scope of the invention. For instance, it is not necessary that the support wall 6 extends perpendicularly from the bottom wall 5. Also, it is to be understood that the transition surface 14 can be composed of a number of surface segments with varying size of the radii.

claim.claim-text: 1. Tool for parting or similar turning operations comprising a holder shaped as a relatively thin disc or disc-shaped portion (1) of a first material such as steel, and a cutting insert (2) of a second harder material such as cemented carbide, whereby said disc-shaped holder (1) at least at one free end is provided with an outwardly open recess

(4) and a rear slot (8) wherein said recess (4) is confined by a bottom wall (5), an inner or rear wall (6) and an upper wall (7) which is part of an elastic movable clamping arm (3) integral with said holder arranged to fasten the insert in the recess, said insert having both upper and lower grooves (11, 12) or alternatively ridges essentially V-shaped in cross-section arranged to cooperate with correspondingly in cross-section V-shaped ridges or alternative ridges adjacent said recess, characterized in, that the rear support wall is in the shape of a support surface (6) which in relation to the bottom wall

(5) extends upwards and in its upper part extends into a convexly shaped surface (14) with relatively large radius (Ri) which extends into a partial surface (15) with essentially smaller radius (R2) which at an inflexion point (16) extends into a concave curved surface (8a) which defines the end of the rear slot (8).

2. Tool as defined in claim 1 , characterized in, that the insert (2) supporting bottom wall next to the rear support wall (6) extends into a recessed by milling produced groove (5 a) of smoothly rounded contour.
3. Tool according to claim 1 or 2, characterized in, that the radius (R) of the milled groove (8a) is approximately equal to or larger than radius (R4) of said milled groove (5a).

4. Tool according to any of the claims 1-3, characterized in, that the rear end surface of the insert (2), which is intended to be supported against the upwardly extending support wall (6), is provided with a V-shaped recess and that the support wall (6) is provided with a corresponding V-shaped extension such that the insert (2) and the support wall (6) together provide a rear male-female joint.
